3) Laura to prepare an internal checklist for procurement/legal handoff so we can route the DocuSign envelope quickly.

All —

Quick commercial flag from my side: Skylift's ask for an explicit UK data residency carve could trigger our EU/UK hosting surcharge in the Order Form (standard uplift is 12% on net MRC for region-locking). I need a confirmation from procurement whether Skylift wants a managed UK-only environment or the hosting will be through our EU region with contractual residency guarantees. If they want managed UK pools, ops needs a 6–8 week lead time for capacity.

Also please note: adding an explicit 30-day erasure period for trial data may require us to add a limited data-extract/archival process in the SOW — Karthik, is that something legal needs to tie into the data processing clause or can we keep it solely in the Order Form?

I'll be on the 8/12 call — can speak to pricing options and timelines.

Thanks,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Desai <external-counsel@rjm-law.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: DPA redline and SCCs crosswalk (draft)

Alice / Grace —

Attached is our initial DPA redline and an SCCs crosswalk (RJM Legal also included suggested language in a separate file). Summary of what we changed:
- Added explicit reference to "Annex B — SCCs" with a clause that the SCCs are incorporated by reference and shall govern transfers to processors headquartered outside the EU/UK.
- Defined data categories and tied the 30-day erasure ask to "Trial Participant Personal Data" only; retained higher risk categories (PHI) under a 90-day hold to enable audit and regulatory reporting.
- Clarified subprocessors flow: Redwood will notify 30 days prior for material subprocessor changes; non-material changes (new minor analytics subprocessor) will be displayed in a public subprocessor list updated monthly.

Outstanding legal points for Skylift:
- Whether you will accept our recommended 90-day PHI hold for auditability; if not, we need explicit confirmation to reduce the PHI retention and update our compliance controls.
- Whether DocuSign signature order should place Redwood as signer 2 (preferred) or signer 1.

Next steps: Priya, could you review the draft clauses below and indicate any redlines you'd like to propose back to Skylift? Aim: have a consolidated redline by 8/16 so procurement can sign off.

Attached: DPA_Redline_v1.docx, RJM_Skylift_Suggested_Clause.txt

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

(Attachment stubs: DPA_Redline_v1.docx [docx], RJM_Skylift_Suggested_Clause.txt [txt])

From: Priya Desai <external-counsel@rjm-law.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alice Moran <alice@skyliftpharma.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline and SCCs crosswalk (draft)

Karthik / Alice —

Quick notes after an initial read:
- Annex B phrasing looks good, but recommend adding a short "conflict resolution" sentence that if any SCC provision contradicts specific MSA obligations, the parties will negotiate in good faith and escalate to the GC level. This prevents downstream enforcement arguments.
- On data retention: accepting a split (30-day for Trial Participant PD / 90-day for PHI) is reasonable. Suggest we add a short operational definition for "Trial Participant Personal Data" so both sides are aligned on scope.
- Subprocessor notifications: 30 days is customary; suggest keeping the monthly public list for transparency. No objections.

I will mark up DPA_Redline_v1.docx and return redlines by EOD 8/17. If Redwood is open to a 60-day PHI hold compromise we could speed execution.

Regards,
Priya Desai
RJM Legal (external counsel for Skylift)
external-counsel@rjm-law.com
